key_insight: The paper shows that token merging in diffusion models should not rely only on text-aligned foreground regions; diffusion dynamics can reveal which tokens are actually important to preserve. By using the model’s own generation behavior, it aims to merge more safely while keeping image quality high.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of speeding up diffusion-based image generation with token merging without harming important visual details. The core issue is deciding which tokens are redundant and which should be kept, especially when background objects matter too.
method: Analyze diffusion dynamics to estimate token importance beyond simple prompt-text alignment.
Identify tokens that can be merged safely while preserving tokens that contribute to meaningful structures, including background content.
Use a training-free strategy to accelerate generation with minimal degradation in output quality.
impact: This helps practitioners reduce compute cost and latency in diffusion image generation while maintaining visual fidelity. It is especially useful for deploying faster generative systems without retraining large models.
visual_elements: Token map highlighting mergeable vs. preserved tokens

paper_title: Which Tokens to Merge? Diffusion Dynamics for Efficient Image Generation
paper_authors: SeungJu Cha, Ye-Chan Kim, HyunGee Kim, Sungho Koh, Dong-Jin Kim
